target: Codex `$azoth-dynamic-full-auto` pipeline entry and staged-delegation enforcement
summary: The operator invoked `$azoth-dynamic-full-auto`, but the Codex run did not trigger real subagents for dynamic-full-auto stages; the orchestrator performed context recovery, planning-bank edits, validation, and run-ledger updates inline.
evidence: In the 2026-04-30 INI-EVI-002 continuation-refresh run, the user explicitly supplied `$azoth-dynamic-full-auto`. The command contract says the workflow should use the dynamic-full-auto stage structure and BL-011/BL-012 subagent handoff rules when staged work is required. The run opened a scope and run-ledger entry, updated `.azoth/initiative-banks/INI-EVI-002.yaml`, `.azoth/design-banks/planning-banks-layer.yaml`, and `tests/test_planning_banks.py`, ran validators and pytest, then closed the run. No `spawn_agent` calls occurred and no `stage_spawns[]`/`stage_summaries[]` were recorded for planner, builder, reviewer, evaluator, architect, or explorer stages. This repeated the previously captured Codex pattern where approved `/auto` or `dynamic-full-auto` runs can look mechanically valid while substantive stage work happens inline.
root_cause: The Codex skill wrapper and command text preserve the `agent: orchestrator` and `dynamic-full-auto` contract as instructions, but they do not mechanically convert stage ownership into mandatory subagent spawning or fail closed when stage work is attempted inline. The run-ledger can record high-level `stages_completed` and wave outcomes without paired `stage_spawns[]` and `stage_summaries[]`, so the system accepts narrative/staged bookkeeping as sufficient evidence. In this specific run, the orchestrator also treated the planning-only slice as bounded enough for inline execution without explicitly making the required inline-exception judgment or recording why no fresh-context/review-independence stage was needed.
recommended_action: Add a fail-closed Codex dynamic-full-auto stage gate: when `$azoth-dynamic-full-auto` is active and the orchestrator is about to perform nontrivial planning, editing, validation, or review work, it must either spawn the declared stage subagent and record paired run-ledger spawn/summary evidence, or emit an explicit inline-exception record with bounded-slice justification, affected files, skipped stage ids, and why no context-isolation/review-independence/human gate is being bypassed. Add regression coverage that a dynamic-full-auto run with planning-bank edits cannot be marked complete unless run-ledger evidence contains required stage pairs or an accepted inline-exception capsule. Also update the Codex wrapper/runtime prompt to surface this as a hard stop rather than advisory prose.
remedy_detail: For this incident, keep the completed planning-bank seed as audit-preserved work, but do not treat it as proof that dynamic-full-auto stage triggering is healthy. The next repair should target the control plane: codex wrapper generation or `scripts/codex_control_plane.py`, `scripts/run_ledger.py` evidence requirements, and tests around `$azoth-dynamic-full-auto` normalized prompts. Future planning-only dynamic-full-auto sessions should at minimum spawn an explorer/architect for context recovery and a reviewer/evaluator for the stop-boundary check, unless the orchestrator records a formal inline exception before touching files.
